entries.question_text:
Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below.
Eight boxes viz. A, B, C, D, E, F, G, and H were placed on a circular table such that all of them are facing
towards the centre, but not necessarily in the same order. Each box has diﬀerent chocolates viz. Barone,
Fuse, Kismi, Kitkat, Lotte, Melody, Munch, and Perk but not necessarily in the same order. 
Not more than two boxes were placed between box H and the box with Fuse when counted from the right
of box H. Box F was placed third to the right of the box with Fuse. Two boxes are placed between box F
and the box with Lotte which is placed to the immediate right of the box with Melody. Box E is placed to
the immediate right of box H.Box G was placed second to the right of box E. The number of boxes
between box E and the box with Lotte is the same as the number of boxes between box F and the box with
Munch, both when counted from the left of the boxes E and F. Box C was placed second to the left of box
D which doesn’t have munch in it. The box with Perk was placed adjacent to the box with Kitkat and box
A which is placed second to the left of the box with Kismi. Odd number of boxes are placed between box
B and Box C on either side.

Q1. Which of the following box has Lotte chocolate?

options.A: The box which is placed second to the right of box C
options.B: The box which is placed to the immediate right of box A
options.C: The box which is placed second to the left of box E
options.D: The box which is placed third to the left of box F

entries.explanation: The unique clockwise arrangement places Lotte in box H. Box H is immediately to the right of A, so option B identifies it.
entries.source: Mains_Topic_wise_Circular_Based_Arrangement_Two_Variable_Facing.pdf; physical PDF page 1; printed question 1; Two-variable box and chocolate arrangement.

Study the following information carefully and answer the below questions.
Eight persons- I, J, K, L, M, N, O, and P are sitting at the circular table facing the center. They are
diﬀerent age persons. All the information is not necessarily in the same order.

Topic-Wise Bundle Course
Mains Topic wise Circular Based Arrangement Two Variable Facing
Inside Set -1
PDF Course Subscription | Mock Tests Subscription | All in One Subscription
Page 3 Of 27
K sits second to the left of the one whose age is 49.J sits opposite to the one who sits immediate right of
P.Neither J’s age nor P’s age is an odd number.  P does not sit opposite to K.The one whose age is 38 sits
second to the left of J.M sits second to the left of the one who sits immediate right of I. I and P are not
immediate neighbors. I’s age is not 38.M does not sit opposite to K.O is eleven years younger than M.The
age diﬀerence between P and I is the same as the age diﬀerence between O and K.K is younger than O.P is

years more than the age diﬀerence between L and K.The age diﬀerence between L and O is not more than
ﬁve years. The sum of the age of K and P is equal to the age of N.

Q6. In which of the following statement, the persons are sitting adjacent to each other? I. PM II. KN III. JO IV. NI
entries.explanation: The unique arrangement makes P adjacent to M and K adjacent to N; J/O and N/I are not adjacent. Only statements I and II hold, option B.
entries.source: Mains_Topic_wise_Circular_Based_Arrangement_Two_Variable_Facing.pdf; physical PDF page 2; printed question 6; Two-variable circular seating with ages.

entries.question_text:
Study the following information carefully and answer the below questions.
Nine persons – B, D, F, H, K, M, Q, T, and W are sitting in a circular table in such a way that some are
facing center whereas other sits facing away from the center. All the information is not necessary in the
same order.
M sits third to the right of K, who sits facing away from the center. W sits third to the left of T, both are
not facing in the same direction. One person sits between Q and K. Neither Q nor M sits adjacent to W.
Neither K nor Q sits adjacent to T. D neither sits adjacent to Q nor T. H sits second to the right of F but
sits facing in the same direction as B. A person who sits immediate left of F sits fourth to the right of D.
Both F and D are facing in the same direction. The persons sitting adjacent to H sit facing in the opposite
direction. Not more than two adjacent persons are facing in the same direction. F sits adjacent to K and H
sits adjacent to W.

Q1. What is the position of B with respect to D?
entries.explanation: D faces the centre, and B is three seats to D's right, option D.
entries.source: Mains_Topic_wise_Circular_Based_Arrangement_Bi_directional_Set_1.pdf; physical PDF page 1; printed question 1; Nine-person bidirectional circular seating.

entries.question_text:

Nine persons – B, D, F, H, K, M, Q, T, and W are sitting in a circular table in such a way that some are
facing center whereas other sits facing away from the center. All the information is not necessary in the
same order.
M sits third to the right of K, who sits facing away from the center. W sits third to the left of T, both are
not facing in the same direction. One person sits between Q and K. Neither Q nor M sits adjacent to W.
Neither K nor Q sits adjacent to T. D neither sits adjacent to Q nor T. H sits second to the right of F but
sits facing in the same direction as B. A person who sits immediate left of F sits fourth to the right of D.
Both F and D are facing in the same direction. The persons sitting adjacent to H sit facing in the opposite
direction. Not more than two adjacent persons are facing in the same direction. F sits adjacent to K and H
sits adjacent to W.

Q2. How many persons are sitting between M and the one who sits immediate right of Q when counted to the right of M?

options.B: As many as between T and F when counted to the left of F.
options.D: As many as between the one who sits second to the right of W and K when counted to the left of K.

entries.explanation: The person immediately right of Q is F. Four people lie from M to F on M's right; neither numeric option nor either comparison option gives four, so option E.
entries.source: Mains_Topic_wise_Circular_Based_Arrangement_Bi_directional_Set_1.pdf; physical PDF page 1; printed question 2; Nine-person bidirectional circular seating.

Study the following information carefully and answer the below questions
Eight persons- L, M, N, O, P, Q, R and S are sitting at the circular table. Four of them are facing the
centre and four of them are facing opposite to the centre. Not more than two adjacent persons are facing
the same direction. All the information is not necessarily in the same order.
N sits opposite to the one who sits second to the left of Q. Two persons are sitting between N and L. M sits
adjacent to neither L nor N. M and Q are not sitting opposite to each other. The number of persons sitting
between M and L is the same as between L and S. P sits immediate left of the one who sits immediate left
of R. R and Q are facing the same direction. S and L are facing the same direction. The one who sits
second to the left of S is facing the opposite direction of R. The immediate neighbours of N are facing
opposite directions to each other. N does not face towards the centre.

Q6. What is the position of S with respect to R?
entries.explanation: R faces the centre. S is five seats to R's right, equivalent to third to the left on this eight-person circle, option D.
entries.source: Mains_Topic_wise_Circular_Based_Arrangement_Bi_directional_Set_1.pdf; physical PDF page 2; printed question 6; Eight-person bidirectional circular seating.

entries.explanation: N is immediately left of S and L immediately left of R; O is not immediately left of Q. Thus I and III only are true, option A.
